newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares end firm, power sector rallies.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares end firm, power sector rallies.

text.p: Ignoring Wall Street's slide, Chilean blue chips closed firmer in thin trade with the market buoyed by hopes of lower domestic interest rates, said traders.
The bolsa is seen opening steady next week although attention will be focussed on the Federal Reserve's policy meeting May 20, they said.

"The Chile market will remain well supported but the big issue next week will be how Latin America reacts to the Fed," said one trader. The 40-share index ended unofficially up 0.87 percent at 119.85 points.
The general index gained 0.41 percent to 5,356.71 points. Turnover shrank slightly to 7.2 billion pesos from 8.5 billion pesos Thursday.
"We've seen a lackluster market in the last couple of days. Now it's popped a little, but we're still in the trading range," said one dealer.

Traders said investors were optimistic that the Central Bank will continue to cut interest rates following comments from leading economists that inflation may below the government's target of 5.5 percent for the year.
Winners included electricity stocks which climbed on forecasts of rainfall this weekend which may ease the water shortages at most of the country's hydroelectric dams, said dealers.
Chile's largest generator Endesa climbed 1.57 percent at 258 pesos while Enersis was up 1.38 percent at 258 pesos.
Losers included telecom Telex down 1.92 percent at 1,020 pesos and supermarket chain Unimarc which lost 0.65 percent to 154 pesos.
